canonical_data: Local SQLite database (better-sqlite3) and OS app-data directory holding agent memory, schedules, and session state
current_repo_note: Most recent commit and release (v1.9.40) are from 2026-06-30, about ten weeks before verification; several issues opened since then (through early September 2026) show no visible maintainer follow-up as of this review.
strengths: Coordinates delegation across 24+ providers and multiple external CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, and others), plus OpenClaw gateways
Orchestration primitives (branching, parallel joins, restart-safe run state) support durable multi-agent workflows, not just single request/response calls
Approval gates, an Eval Lab, and an Operations Pulse dashboard give operators visibility and control over running agent fleets
Ships as desktop app, npm global CLI, and self-hosted Docker/PaaS images, all under one MIT license
weaknesses: No commit or release since 2026-06-30 (v1.9.40) as of this review, roughly ten weeks with several unaddressed issues opened afterward
Optional agent-linked crypto wallet features (Solana/Ethereum signing) widen the security surface beyond a typical agent runtime
Production-readiness claims ("used in production by teams") are vendor-asserted in the README FAQ with no independent corroboration
Shares an owner with a separate candidate (swarmvault) under review elsewhere; this review relies only on swarmclaw's own repository evidence
why_it_matters: A control-plane layer for coordinating swarms of delegated agents and external CLI/gateway backends, distinct from single-agent personal runtimes like the OpenClaw it explicitly integrates with.
